content.text:
**The digest direction is confirmed right — and this time I found the remaining hole myself, before spending a panel round on it** (comment 4885226805).

What I verified at `28e9b7de5`: every prescribed probe dies on the digest — GPT's never-true condition on both lanes, a one-character comment edit — each failing loud with an error that names the constant to bump. The mechanism works.

What I found: the digest check **fails open when its anchor disappears**. If the step can't be found by name, the check silently returns no errors — and nothing else pins the step names. I proved the full bypass: rename the step, then neuter the log tail behind a no-op colon (which keeps the old fragment pins satisfied) — verifier completely green. The digest was the terminating pattern, but its lookup path reintroduced enumeration through the back door. Same principle as the poison-lock fix at the top of this repo's history: recovery and lookup paths must fail closed too.

Relay to Codex:

> "PR #1232 round 5 — my finding, see comment 4885226805, fix is mechanical: (1) in `partition_run_body_digest_errors`, `run_body is None` must emit `{label}: digest pin target step not found` instead of returning [] — fail closed, both lanes; (2) per-lane self-test mutation renaming the pinned step and expecting exactly that error. No other changes. Re-run verifier + hygiene self-test, push, report head SHA."

Why this round is different from the previous ones, since you asked about direction: rounds 1–3 were enumeration probing enumeration — unbounded. The digest bounded it: body edits are now *provably* covered (any byte, any shape), and the anchor is the single remaining degree of freedom. Close that with fail-closed-on-missing and there is nothing left to probe in this class — which is also why I'm confident calling round 5 the last code round. After it: one confirmation panel at final head, exact-head CI, your approval.
